module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Beck–Fiala theorem and conjecture

Discrepancy of bounded-degree set systems. Given sets $S_1, \dots, S_m \subseteq [n]$
such that every element of $[n]$ belongs to at most $t$ of the sets (the system has
*degree* at most $t$), one seeks a colouring $\chi \colon [n] \to \{-1, +1\}$ making
every set as balanced as possible, i.e. minimizing the *discrepancy*
$\max_i \left|\sum_{j \in S_i} \chi(j)\right|$.

The Beck–Fiala theorem (1981) states that every set system of degree at most $t \ge 1$
has discrepancy at most $2t - 1$. The Beck–Fiala conjecture asserts that the truth is
much stronger: the discrepancy of a degree-$t$ system is $O(\sqrt{t})$, with a constant
independent of $n$, $m$ and $t$.

Despite considerable attention the bound $2t - 1$ has been improved only slightly:
Bukh (2016) proved a bound of the form $2t - \log^* t$ (where $\log^*$ is the iterated
logarithm), and Banaszczyk's vector balancing theorem yields $O(\sqrt{t \log n})$.
The Komlós conjecture (see `KomlosConjecture.lean`) would imply the Beck–Fiala
conjecture, since scaling the incidence vectors of a degree-$t$ system by $1/\sqrt{t}$
produces vectors of Euclidean norm at most $1$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beck%E2%80%93Fiala_theorem)
- [J. Beck and T. Fiala, *"Integer-making" theorems*,
  Discrete Applied Mathematics **3** (1981), 1–8](https://doi.org/10.1016/0166-218X(81)90022-6)
- [B. Bukh, *An improvement of the Beck–Fiala theorem*,
  Combinatorics, Probability and Computing **25** (2016), 380–398](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0963548315000140)
- [W. Banaszczyk, *Balancing vectors and Gaussian measures of n-dimensional convex bodies*,
  Random Structures & Algorithms **12** (1998), 351–360](https://doi.org/10.1002/(SICI)1098-2418(199807)12:4%3C351::AID-RSA3%3E3.0.CO;2-S)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace BeckFiala

/--
**The Beck–Fiala theorem**

If $S_1, \dots, S_m \subseteq [n]$ is a set system of degree at most $t$, i.e. every
$j \in [n]$ lies in at most $t$ of the sets, and $t \ge 1$, then there is a colouring
$\chi \colon [n] \to \{-1, +1\}$ with $\left|\sum_{j \in S_i} \chi(j)\right| \le 2t - 1$
for every $i$.

The hypothesis $t \ge 1$ is necessary: a system of degree $0$ consists of empty sets
only, whose discrepancy is $0 > 2 \cdot 0 - 1$.

[J. Beck and T. Fiala, *"Integer-making" theorems*,
Discrete Applied Mathematics **3** (1981), 1–8.]
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/Lemmy00/beck-fiala-lean/blob/19334973121b07e428c51e15b914e9ca4921fbb9/BeckFialaProof/BeckFiala.lean#L35"]
theorem beck_fiala_theorem (n m t : ℕ) (ht : 1 ≤ t) (S : Fin m → Finset (Fin n))
    (hdeg : ∀ j, (Finset.univ.filter fun i => j ∈ S i).card ≤ t) :
    ∃ χ : Fin n → ℝ, (∀ j, χ j = 1 ∨ χ j = -1) ∧
      ∀ i, |∑ j ∈ S i, χ j| ≤ 2 * (t : ℝ) - 1 := by
  sorry

/--
**The Beck–Fiala conjecture**

There exists a universal constant $C > 0$ such that every set system
$S_1, \dots, S_m \subseteq [n]$ of degree at most $t$ admits a colouring
$\chi \colon [n] \to \{-1, +1\}$ with
$\left|\sum_{j \in S_i} \chi(j)\right| \le C \sqrt{t}$ for every $i$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem beck_fiala_conjecture :
    ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ (n m t : ℕ) (S : Fin m → Finset (Fin n)),
      (∀ j, (Finset.univ.filter fun i => j ∈ S i).card ≤ t) →
      ∃ χ : Fin n → ℝ, (∀ j, χ j = 1 ∨ χ j = -1) ∧
        ∀ i, |∑ j ∈ S i, χ j| ≤ C * Real.sqrt t := by
  sorry

/--
Sanity check: a system with no sets at all ($m = 0$) admits any colouring vacuously;
in particular the all-ones colouring satisfies every discrepancy bound.
-/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem beck_fiala_conjecture.variants.no_sets (n t : ℕ) (S : Fin 0 → Finset (Fin n))
    (_hdeg : ∀ j, (Finset.univ.filter fun i => j ∈ S i).card ≤ t) :
    ∃ χ : Fin n → ℝ, (∀ j, χ j = 1 ∨ χ j = -1) ∧
      ∀ i, |∑ j ∈ S i, χ j| ≤ Real.sqrt t :=
  ⟨fun _ => 1, fun _ => Or.inl rfl, fun i => i.elim0⟩

end BeckFiala

status_issues.recorded: @[category research open, AMS 5]. The module docstring still says the Komlós conjecture "would imply" Beck–Fiala and that the 2t − 1 bound "has been improved only slightly".
status_issues.source_status: Solved in September 2026, as a corollary of the proof of the Komlós conjecture. S. Guo, E. X. Fang and J. Lu, arXiv:2609.11189 (v1 10 Sep 2026), prove Komlós with constant 3√(2π). Their Corollary "Beck–Fiala bound" says: for positive integers m, n, t, if A ∈ {0,1}^{m×n} has at most t nonzero entries in each column, then disc(A) < 3√(2πt). S. R. Karingula and S. Lovett, arXiv:2609.20979 (v1 17 Sep 2026), give an elementary proof of Komlós with K = 36, which gives Beck–Fiala with C = 36.
status_issues.evidence: Abstract of arXiv:2609.11189: "As a consequence, every finite set system in which each element belongs to at most t sets, where t≥1 is an integer, admits a two-coloring whose imbalance in each set is less than 3√(2πt). This gives the square-root dependence predicted by the Beck-Fiala conjecture." The LaTeX source has \begin{corollary}[Beck--Fiala bound] with the proof "Every column of A/√t has Euclidean norm at most one, so Theorem [Komlós] gives disc(A)=√t disc(A/√t)<3√(2πt)." Abstract of arXiv:2609.20979: "any vectors v_1,…,v_n∈R^d with ‖v_i‖_2≤1 admit signs ε_i∈{−1,1} such that ‖∑ε_i v_i‖_∞≤36." In the same commit, FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/KomlosConjecture.lean already tags `komlos_conjecture` as `research solved` with a `formal_proof` record (local commit 2f82a241, 2026-09-21, #6450, "formalise the Karingula–Lovett proof"). This file was last changed on 2026-09-18 and never updated. In a scratch file I proved in Lean (about 40 lines, sorry-free apart from the hypothesis) that `type_of% KomlosConjecture.komlos_conjecture → type_of% BeckFiala.beck_fiala_conjecture`, with the same constant: scale the incidence vectors by 1/√t and treat t = 0 separately, where all sets are empty. Wikipedia's Beck–Fiala page does not yet record the resolution. As of 23 Sep 2026 it only says "Beck and Fiala conjectured that the imbalance can be even bounded by O(√t)".

reformulations.difference: The source (Wikipedia; Bukh: "Beck and Fiala conjectured that f(d)=O(√d)") states an asymptotic O(√t) bound. The Lean statement asks for a single constant C > 0 that works for every t : ℕ, including t = 0 and small t.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The uniform version trivially implies the eventual one (take t₀ = 0). Conversely, suppose disc ≤ C√t for all t ≥ t₀. For 1 ≤ t < t₀ the Beck–Fiala theorem gives disc ≤ 2t − 1 ≤ 2t₀ ≤ 2t₀√t. For t = 0 the degree bound forces every set to be empty, so the discrepancy is 0 ≤ C'·0. So C' = max(C, 2t₀) works for all t. I proved the ↔ in Lean between an "∃ C > 0, ∃ t₀, ∀ t ≥ t₀, …" statement and `type_of% BeckFiala.beck_fiala_conjecture`, taking `type_of% BeckFiala.beck_fiala_theorem` as a hypothesis. That theorem has a verified external formal proof.

review.notes:
No misformalizations found. The file has three declarations, all checked against the sources and in Lean.

1. `beck_fiala_theorem` matches the Wikipedia statement exactly: a family S₁…Sₘ ⊆ [n] in which every element lies in at most t sets has a ±1 colouring with every |x(S_j)| ≤ 2t − 1.
   - The only extra hypothesis is `1 ≤ t`, and it is necessary. I proved in Lean that the statement without it is false at t = 0, n = 0, m = 1 (one empty set: 0 > −1). The docstring explains this.
   - `2t − 1` is the right uniform bound. I checked in Lean that it is attained at t = 1 by a single singleton set. Bukh's paper credits Beck–Fiala with 2d − 2, but that bound can only hold for d ≥ 2. Guo–Fang–Lu also describe the classical bound as 2t − 1.
   - Indexing the sets as `Fin m → Finset (Fin n)` allows repeated sets, with degree counted with multiplicity. This is the source's indexed collection S₁…Sₘ, and it is equivalent to the set-family version by deduplication.
   - The `formal_proof` link checks out. The linked theorem at line 35 is a verbatim copy of the statement. The external repo uses the same toolchain and Mathlib (v4.33.1). I concatenated its nine files, compiled them here, and confirmed that `example : type_of% @BeckFiala.beck_fiala_theorem := @BeckFiala.beck_fiala_theorem_ext` typechecks. `#print axioms` shows only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].

2. `beck_fiala_conjecture` is the standard statement: ∃ C > 0, ∀ n m t S, if the degree is at most t then some ±1 colouring has discrepancy ≤ C√t.
   - The t = 0 and n = 0 cases are harmless, since all sets are then empty and every sum is 0.
   - The statement is not trivial. It follows from the repo's Komlós statement with the same constant (proved in scratch).
   - The only problem is the stale `research open` tag, reported under status_issues. The module docstring's wording about Komlós and about "only slight" improvements is stale in the same way.

3. `beck_fiala_conjecture.variants.no_sets` is a vacuous m = 0 test, correctly proved and correctly tagged `test`.

I did not consult the external fork (mo271/formal-conjectures) that KomlosConjecture.lean cites as its formal proof. It is a copy of this repository, and the status issue does not depend on it: the arXiv papers settle it. I also could not read the full text of the 1981 Beck–Fiala paper (ScienceDirect returns 403). This does not affect the verdict: the cited Wikipedia page, Guo–Fang–Lu's account, and the Semantic Scholar summary all give the 2t − 1 / O(√t) forms that the file states.
